rule:permanent-control-theft.definition: Permanently gains control of a permanent an opponent controls; the effect lasts indefinitely rather than expiring at end of turn or at a stated duration.
rule:permanent-control-theft.note: effect axis. Distinct from rule:temporary-control-theft by DURATION, which is load-bearing: a permanent steal answers a threat forever, a temporary one is a tempo play.

rule:combat-damage-to-player-permanent-c.definition: Whenever this creature deals combat damage to a player, its controller may permanently gain control of a creature that player controls.
rule:combat-damage-to-player-permanent-c.note: compound of combat-damage-to-player delivery with permanent control theft.

rule:optional-self-sacrifice-in-trigger.definition: A triggered ability offers its controller the option to sacrifice the source as a condition of the effect ("you may sacrifice it. If you do, ..."). Distinct from an activation cost: the sacrifice happens on RESOLUTION, not on activation, so grammar section 9's cost-vs-effect law bars it from any -cost- slug.
rule:optional-self-sacrifice-in-trigger.note: deliberately NOT rule:activated-ability-costs-self-sacrifice, which is an activation cost (CR 113.3b, left of the colon).

rule:combat-damage-to-player-forced-owne.definition: Whenever this creature deals combat damage to a player, that player returns a permanent they control to its owner's hand. The AFFECTED PLAYER chooses, not the controller, so the bounce cannot be aimed at a specific threat.
rule:combat-damage-to-player-forced-owne.note: no existing bounce axis fits: targeted-bounce-creature / etb-bounce-other-creature are all YOU bouncing a chosen target.

rule:combat-damage-to-player-draw.definition: Whenever this creature deals combat damage to a player, its controller draws one or more cards, with NO discard attached. Distinct from the -loot sibling: looting is draw-THEN-discard (grammar section 4).

rule:combat-damage-to-player-plus1-count.definition: Whenever this creature deals combat damage to a player, its controller puts a +1/+1 counter on another target creature they control.

rule:combat-damage-to-player-free-cast.definition: Whenever this creature deals combat damage to a player, its controller may cast one or more spells without paying their mana costs.
rule:combat-damage-to-player-free-cast.note: Kotis, the Fangkeeper is a second member waiting -- it is not in the codebook at all and should seed here at the corpus pass.

rule:combat-damage-to-player-mill-oppone.definition: Whenever this creature deals combat damage to a player, that player mills cards.

moves.why: Riptide Entrancer never discards -- it gains control of a creature
draw with no discard; looting is draw-THEN-discard
Prowler puts a +1/+1 counter; it neither draws nor discards
Maelstrom Archangel casts a free spell; it neither draws nor discards
Sword of Body and Mind mills and creates a token; it neither draws nor discards

adds.why: Riptide Entrancer decomposes onto its effect axis as well as the compound
"you may sacrifice it. If you do" -- the cost-condition facet
Blizzard Specter is modal; it holds membership on BOTH modes' axes

definition_edits.rule:temporary-control-theft: Gains control of a target permanent, usually another player's, only UNTIL END OF TURN or for another stated temporary duration. The duration is load-bearing: a steal that lasts indefinitely belongs on rule:permanent-control-theft.
definition_edits.rule:combat-damage-to-player-loot: Whenever this creature deals combat damage to a player, its controller LOOTS -- draws one or more cards and then discards. Both halves are required; a conditional discard still counts, a missing discard does not. Draw-only belongs on rule:combat-damage-to-player-draw.
